RUNAWAY BALLOON'S FALL ON A LONDON HOUSE.

Making preparations to remove the wreckage of a captive balloon which broke away yesterday (April 15th) from its moorings at the Crystal Palace and crashed into a house outside the grounds. It damaged a chimney-stack and Gansco smoked several slates. Jagged brockwork ripped the envelope and let the gas escape.

NEW ITEM-The big navy dirigible left the Montauk naval air situation this morning at 8.00 o'clock on its first lap of its trans Atlantic flight making a stop at Newfoundland. The craft carries two vertical six cylinder motors of the Union type and in a test flight ran ten hours on on ninety gallons of gasoline. The upper photo shows the dirigible while the crew is in the lower. They are from left to right Commander E.V. Oil in command of the ship, Leutenant J.V. Lawrence, Leut.M.H.Easterly and Ensign D.P. Campbell. Photo taken just before the flight while the upper photo shows the dirigible on its way.

NAVY TRAINS AIRMEN TO MAN ITS DRIGIBLES.

Aeroplanes have taken so important a place in warfare that we hear relatively little nowadays of the more cumbersome dirigibles. The lighter than air machines still have their place in warfare and are being used to a considerable extent by our Navy which employs the "Blimp" type. These students at the Naval Aviation Station at Pensacola, Forinda are tuning up the engine of one of the dirigibles they are learning to control. 27/27/18.
